subject: Conditional segmented log erasure & audit sampling — CedarBank
messages:
From: Olivia Marsh <olivia.marsh@cedarbank.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement <procurement@cedarbank.com>
Date: Sat, 30 May 2026 16:12:00 +01:00
Subject: CedarBank logs: segmented erasure and proof of delete

Hi Irene,

Quick question from the compliance team — CedarBank needs to confirm that tenant-scoped debug/trace logs for EU production instances can be erased on a segmented basis (per-tenant) and that we can receive independent proof-of-delete artifacts for a sampled subset of deletions. The baseline ask is:
- 12 month transactional retention for audit traces, but ability to securely erase tenant traces on demand
- Proof-of-delete logs for a 1% sample, with hash digest and timestamped evidence (SOC2-aligned)
- Chain-of-custody notes for any escrowed snapshots taken for investigations

I attached our retention spec (cedarbank-retention-specs.docx) to show constraints from procurement. Can Redwood confirm feasibility and what artifacts you can provide? Also please indicate whether any elevated SLA / addendum is required for this flow.

Thanks,
Olivia Marsh
Senior Compliance Manager
CedarBank

Attachment: cedarbank-retention-specs.docx (docx, 24KB)

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
To: Olivia Marsh <olivia.marsh@cedarbank.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 01 Jun 2026 08:17:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: CedarBank logs: segmented erasure and proof of delete

Hi Olivia —

Thanks for the detail and the spec doc. We can support tenant-scoped segmented erasure in our EU deployment, but there are a few items we need to clarify before providing the formal artifacts:

1) Scope of "debug/trace logs": are we talking ephemeral inference traces (KV cache + transient request traces), or persisted audit logs (request metadata + token-level billing indices)?
2) Desired proof-of-delete cadence and format: you mentioned 1% sampling. Do you require a cryptographic hash for each deleted file plus a notarized timestamp, or will a signed digest bundle and deletion manifest satisfy audit?
3) Escrow snapshots: if CedarBank wants snapshots for forensics, that triggers extra controls (encrypted at rest with KMS separation). Do you want escrow in our managed vault or delivered to CedarBank's escrow partner?

Looping in Karthik for contract/SLAs and Marissa for SOC 2 / evidence packaging. I'll put together an initial retention-summary.pdf and a high-level matrix for the sampling approach.

Best,
Irene Choi
Director, Product Security
Redwood Inference

Attachment: retention-summary.pdf (pdf, 48KB)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Olivia Marsh <olivia.marsh@cedarbank.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 01 Jun 2026 10:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: CedarBank logs: segmented erasure and proof of delete

Hi Olivia — quick one from commercial side.

We have a deal in-flight (DB-4821) and CedarBank's requirement for segmented erasure + evidence is a potential addendum. High level: Redwood can provide the artifacts you describe under an SOC 2 attested workflow. Two practical notes:

- If CedarBank requires notarized third-party attestation for each sampled deletion, that will likely be an add-on (professional services + evidence hosting).
- If you accept a signed digest bundle (SHA256 digests, timestamped, signed by Redwood's Evidence Key) and a deletion manifest for sampled tenants, we can include that under the Dedicated/Private contract with no separate attestation fee.

Proposed next step: a 45-minute technical compliance workshop this week to align scope (trace types + sample cadence) and then we'll capture requirements in an MAA (mutual action plan). If CedarBank procurement is comfortable, we can run the workshop and Redwood will deliver a sample proof-of-delete package within 7 business days.

Irene/Marissa — can you confirm the expected artifacts and whether the sample proof-of-delete approach meets SOC 2 evidence guidelines?

Thanks,
Karthik
Head of Sales, EMEA
Redwood Inference

Attachment: none

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Olivia Marsh <olivia.marsh@cedarbank.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 02 Jun 2026 09:34:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: CedarBank logs: segmented erasure and proof of delete

Hi Olivia —

Appreciate the clear ask. For SOC 2-aligned evidence we typically provide the following artifacts for a sampled erase workflow:

- Signed deletion manifest (JSONL): list of tenant IDs, object paths, SHA256 digest, deletion timestamp, Redwood signature
- Signed digest bundle (.tar.gz + signature): digest bundle for the sample set, with a signed index
- Audit trail extract: extraction of the internal audit log that shows the deletion job run-id, operator id (system account), and KMS key id used to perform the action
- Optional notarized timestamp (third-party) — typically engaged only on high-assurance financial customers

I've attached a tight matrix that maps the artifact to compliance purpose and sample cadence. For CedarBank's 1% request, our standard is to provide: signed manifest + digest bundle + audit trail extract. If you require notarization, we can add that as a PS item.

Two implementation clarifications required from your side:
- Confirm which tenant identifiers you want redacted in the manifest (full tenant id vs. hashed tenant id)
- Confirm whether CedarBank's escrow partner will be receiving the snapshots (and provide partner contact)

Irene's team will handle the retention rules in the EU cluster and provide a runbook for evidence generation.

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Senior Security & Compliance Engineer
Redwood Inference

Attachment: segmented-retention-matrix.xlsx (xlsx, 38KB)
